alternatives: add targeted redundancy around the largest failure modes in public-service continuity under multichannel demand surge
select an adaptive robust portfolio across severe scenarios for public-service continuity under multichannel demand surge

assumptions: Requests, contacts, duplicates, service categories, assignments, work orders, and outcomes remain distinct.
Channel and area comparisons account for taxonomy, access, publication, and reporting differences.
All alternatives, capacities, costs, effects, thresholds, and failure scenarios are proposed until bound to evidence.
design.baseline: apply current continuity provisions to public-service continuity under multichannel demand surge.

constraints.description: The 311 and public-service demand operations stress test must respect declared minimum continuity and safety thresholds across severe scenarios.
Every released metric must retain evidence type, source lineage, geography, time, assumptions, and uncertainty.
No analytical output may bypass lawful authority, accountable human review, or an applicable appeal process.

design.decision_cadence: recompiled at each planning cycle and after material evidence change
design.decision_owner: chief service officer and 311 operations director
design.decision_question: Which intake and field-response plan sustains priority services during event, outage, absence, and channel surges?

independence_key.binding_constraint: The 311 and public-service demand operations stress test must respect declared minimum continuity and safety thresholds across severe scenarios.
independence_key.decision_object: public-service continuity under multichannel demand surge
independence_key.evidence_gate: Evidence for public-service continuity under multichannel demand surge passes documented checks for scenario ranges, dependence, failure rates, recovery, intervention performance, and sensitivity.
independence_key.intervention_mechanism: arrival, channel, workforce, system, and field-capacity simulation
independence_key.primary_outcome: scenario-weighted priority requests beyond response targets

design.intended_claim: A versioned stress-test design for comparing declared alternatives affecting public-service continuity under multichannel demand surge, conditional on its evidence gate.
limitations: This library record has no city binding and therefore reports no local input, output, or recommendation.
Readiness describes explicit source and method gates; it does not certify implementation feasibility.
External domain, legal, community, security, and operational review remains outside this design artifact.

objectives.metric: scenario-weighted priority requests beyond response targets
distributional gap in scenario-weighted priority requests beyond response targets
decision claims with complete evidence lineage

prohibited_claims: Do not present synthetic requests, failures, or response times as observed service performance.
Do not describe a design-only record as a city execution, deployment, adopted policy, or impact result.
Do not relabel proposed, estimated, simulated, optimized, or causal evidence as observed evidence.
Do not infer individual behavior, protected status, harm, or entitlement from aggregate records.

release_gate.failure_release: Release an explicit insufficient-evidence record naming missing sources, failed diagnostics, prohibited claims, and the next validation action.
release_gate.pass_condition: Evidence for public-service continuity under multichannel demand surge passes documented checks for scenario ranges, dependence, failure rates, recovery, intervention performance, and sensitivity.

design.title: Stress-test public-service continuity under demand surge
transportability_risks: Service taxonomies, channels, SLAs, agency ownership, reporting, and publication rules differ.
Observed demand reflects both conditions and ability or willingness to report.

family.affected_system: multichannel public-service intake, triage, dispatch, and resolution workflow
claim_boundary: Service requests measure reported workload, not verified incidents, need, harm, or resolution.
Assignments and schedules are proposed operations, not completed work or public outcomes.
Design records do not establish agency adoption, deployment, productivity, or resident impact.
family.decision_owner: chief service officer and 311 operations director
family.description: Eight decisions for intake-pattern diagnosis, workload forecasting, service improvement, access siting, case allocation, staffing schedules, demand stress, and channel evaluation.
family.title: 311 and public-service demand operations

library_claim_boundary: The catalog contains 240 decision designs, not 240 city executions.
Exactly twelve designs map to existing Tier-D reference templates; 228 remain design-only.
A reference implementation can be an explicit negative release and does not imply impact.
No record claims a city binding, new method, deployment, adoption, or real-user outcome.
Future execution requires source binding, gate passage, and domain, legal, community, and operational review.
